entries.title: Apply phase-49 durable packet render jobs and artifact-gated credit
entries.why: A sponsored packet credit is currently consumed with no validated artifact in existence. packet/generate/route.ts records a credit when packetStatus reaches 'ready', and 'ready' is produced by an in-memory text/plain string with no render, no storage write and no read-back. This migration makes credit movement impossible without stored, checksummed bytes. The migration stays in the canonical supabase/ directory: relocating it would create a fake distinction between the code and the schema it requires.
entries.riskNote: Additive and forward-only. Creates three new tables, one trigger and two functions. Alters no existing table, drops nothing, and backfills nothing. No application code reads these objects yet, so applying it changes no runtime behaviour on its own.

entries.rollback: Documented at the foot of the migration: drop the two functions, the two credit tables, the trigger and its function, then packet_render_jobs. Additive, so no pre-existing row is affected.

entries.title: Apply phase-48 packet render jobs, packet accounting and delivery events
entries.authorizedBy: Roger Roman (RCAP Delivery Gate Prompt v3: the phase-48 Supabase authorization applies on the delivery branch only)
entries.why: The deployed packet path consumed sponsored credit on a status flip with no artifact behind it, and rendering happened inline in a request handler with no retry, no fencing, and no accounting. This migration adds durable render jobs with fencing tokens and retry exhaustion, an append-only packet credit ledger keyed on immutable IDs, atomic finalization that verifies re-read stored bytes before any credit moves, and delivery events written only by the authenticated download route.
entries.riskNote: Additive and forward-only. Creates four new tables, guard triggers, and eleven service functions. Alters no existing table; partner_entitlement and all screening behavior are untouched (EXTEND, not replace). No application code on main reads these objects.

entries.title: Apply phase-50 packet delivery hardening (after phase 49)
entries.authorizedBy: Roger Roman (RCAP Unification Prompt v2: reconciled integration branch and canonical migration path; repository integration only)
entries.why: Reconciles the two packet-delivery lanes. Phase 49 (PR #91, authorized) stays the canonical base; this follow-on adds fencing tokens on every worker-owned mutation, retry exhaustion with terminal dispositions, the atomic finalization transaction with re-read hash verification, transmission-named delivery events written only by the authenticated route, and packet accounting keyed on immutable IDs (partner_id : entitlement_id : person_id : matter_id), superseding phase 49's slug-keyed allocation pair while both are provably unapplied. It also installs the real mutation boundary: runtime roles lose direct DML on the protected tables, so the authority GUC is coordination, not security.
entries.riskNote: Forward-only companion to phase 49; applies only after it in the same sequence. Drops two empty phase-49 accounting tables (documented supersession) and creates the canonical entitlement, ledger and delivery-event tables. Alters no pre-existing production table.
preconditions: phase-49-rcap-packet-render-jobs.sql applied immediately before, in the same authorized window
